objectives.en: List the uses of transgenic animals
Explain the roles of GEAC, patents and the problem of biopiracy

narration.en: In 1997 an American company was granted a patent on a basmati-type rice through the US Patent and Trademark Office. Indian farmers had grown basmati for centuries. Biotechnology raises questions of science and of fairness.
narration.kn: 1997ರಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು ಅಮೆರಿಕನ್ ಕಂಪನಿಗೆ ಅಮೆರಿಕದ ಪೇಟೆಂಟ್ ಕಚೇರಿಯಿಂದ ಬಾಸ್ಮತಿ ಮಾದರಿಯ ಅಕ್ಕಿಗೆ ಪೇಟೆಂಟ್ ಸಿಕ್ಕಿತು. ಭಾರತೀಯ ರೈತರು ಶತಮಾನಗಳಿಂದ ಬಾಸ್ಮತಿ ಬೆಳೆಯುತ್ತಿದ್ದರು. ಜೈವಿಕ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನದ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ನ್ಯಾಯದ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳನ್ನೂ ಎತ್ತುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Animals whose DNA has been manipulated to possess and express an extra (foreign) gene are transgenic animals. Transgenic rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have been produced, but over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice. They are made for: (i) normal physiology and development: studying how genes are regulated and how they affect normal body functions, for example insulin-like growth factor; (ii) study of disease: as models for human diseases such as cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis and Alzheimer's; (iii) biological products: for example human protein α-1-antitrypsin, used to treat emphysema; similar attempts for phenylketonuria and cystic fibrosis. In 1997 the first transgenic cow, Rosie, produced human protein-enriched milk (2.4 grams per litre) containing human alpha-lactalbumin, nutritionally more balanced for human babies than natural cow milk; (iv) vaccine safety: transgenic mice are used to test the safety of the polio vaccine before human use; (v) chemical safety testing (toxicity testing): animals made more sensitive to toxic substances give results in less time.

points.en: Disease models: cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis, Alzheimer's
Rosie (1997): milk with human alpha-lactalbumin, 2.4 g/L
Polio vaccine safety tested in transgenic mice

narration.en: Transgenic animals carry a foreign gene; most are mice. They help us study normal development and diseases, make proteins like alpha-1-antitrypsin, test vaccine and chemical safety, and in 1997 the cow Rosie gave milk containing human alpha-lactalbumin.
narration.kn: ಕುಲಾಂತರಿ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಹೊರಗಿನ ಜೀನ್ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ; ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನವು ಇಲಿಗಳು. ಅವು ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ ಮತ್ತು ರೋಗಗಳ ಅಧ್ಯಯನ, ಆಲ್ಫಾ-1-ಆಂಟಿಟ್ರಿಪ್ಸಿನ್‌ನಂತಹ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ, ಲಸಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ರಾಸಾಯನಿಕ ಸುರಕ್ಷತಾ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗೆ ಸಹಾಯಕ; 1997ರಲ್ಲಿ ರೋಸಿ ಹಸು ಮಾನವ ಆಲ್ಫಾ-ಲ್ಯಾಕ್ಟಾಲ್ಬುಮಿನ್ ಇರುವ ಹಾಲು ನೀಡಿತು.

body.en: Manipulating living organisms can have unpredictable results when they are introduced into an ecosystem, so the Indian Government has set up organisations such as GEAC (Genetic Engineering Approval Committee), which decides on the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM organisms for public services. Problems also arise when patents are granted for products and technologies that use genetic materials, plants and other biological resources identified, developed and used for a long time by farmers and indigenous people of a country. India has 27 documented varieties of basmati rice, and in 1997 an American company got patent rights on basmati rice through the US Patent and Trademark Office. Biopiracy is the term used for the use of bio-resources by multinational companies and other organisations without proper authorisation from the countries and people concerned, without compensatory payment. Some nations are developing laws to prevent such unauthorised exploitation; the Indian Parliament has cleared the second amendment of the Indian Patents Bill, which takes such issues into consideration.

points.en: GEAC: approves GM research and release in India
India has 27 documented basmati varieties; US patent granted in 1997
Biopiracy: use of bio-resources without authorisation or compensation

narration.en: GEAC decides whether GM research and GM organisms are safe for use in India. Biopiracy means companies using a country's biological resources or traditional knowledge without permission or payment, as in the basmati patent case.
narration.kn: ಭಾರತದಲ್ಲಿ GM ಸಂಶೋಧನೆ ಮತ್ತು GM ಜೀವಿಗಳ ಸುರಕ್ಷತೆಯನ್ನು GEAC ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಬಾಸ್ಮತಿ ಪೇಟೆಂಟ್ ಪ್ರಕರಣದಂತೆ, ಒಂದು ದೇಶದ ಜೈವಿಕ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲ ಅಥವಾ ಸಾಂಪ್ರದಾಯಿಕ ಜ್ಞಾನವನ್ನು ಅನುಮತಿ ಅಥವಾ ಪರಿಹಾರವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಬಳಸುವುದೇ ಜೈವಿಕ ಕಳ್ಳತನ.

problem.en: A foreign company collects a medicinal plant used for generations by a tribal community in the Western Ghats, patents a drug made from it, and pays nothing to the community or to India. Name this practice and the steps India has taken against it.

steps.en: The company is using a bio-resource and traditional knowledge without authorisation or compensation.
India has amended its patent law (the second amendment of the Indian Patents Bill) to address such issues.

answer.en: Biopiracy; India responded with the second amendment of the Indian Patents Bill.

points.en: GEAC regulates GM organisms; biopiracy is use of bio-resources without consent or payment.
points.kn: GEAC GM ಜೀವಿಗಳನ್ನು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಒಪ್ಪಿಗೆ ಅಥವಾ ಪರಿಹಾರವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಜೈವಿಕ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲ ಬಳಕೆಯೇ ಜೈವಿಕ ಕಳ್ಳತನ.
